shortDescription: Amazon NASDAQ:AMZN, Alphabet's Google NASDAQ:GOOGL and Intel NASDAQ:INTC are joining a technology-led education initiative backed by First Lady Melania Trump, with participating companies committing more than $23 million in resources, tools and expertise to expand access to artificial intelligence…

children: are joining a technology-led education initiative backed by First Lady Melania Trump, with participating companies committing more than $23 million in resources, tools and expertise to expand access to artificial intelligence education worldwide. The agreements highlight another avenue for major technology companies to introduce their AI products to students and educators as competition for adoption intensifies.
The White House said Wednesday that Adobe
and Zoom (ZM) are participating through new private-sector partnerships under the Fostering the Future Together initiative.
The commitments combine financial support, technology access and educational resources rather than representing exclusively direct cash contributions.
Among the largest initiatives, Amazon plans to expand free access to its Kiro AI coding assistant, targeting 5 million students across 132 universities.
Its AWS Academy will separately provide free training opportunities to more than 2 million students.
Google has committed $4 million to expanding its AI-focused Educator Series internationally, while Intel plans to deploy technology across 10 countries.
Adobe will provide students worldwide with free AI-powered study and creative tools through Student Spaces.
Zoom Cares, meanwhile, is allocating $2.75 million in AI for Good grants across Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Asia-Pacific region.
The agreements build on Fostering the Future Together's broader mission of expanding children's access to technology, education and digital skills through international public-private partnerships.
For participating companies, the immediate financial significance of the commitments is likely less important than their potential to expand product adoption.
Amazon and Google, in particular, could introduce their respective AI and cloud ecosystems to millions of students and future technology professionals.
Investors should monitor actual enrollment, platform usage and whether expanded educational access translates into sustained institutional adoption.
However, these commitments should not be mistaken for guaranteed future commercial revenue, and their direct earnings impact on the participating technology giants remains unquantified.

title: Amazon, Google Make $23 Million Education Pledge
